criteria.limit_once: Demand a single PARAM token carrying the row-limit number, with the top-level LimitCount pointing at that same reference. Repeat appearances fail the descriptor, so the LIMIT value supplied at the call site never leaks into predicates.
criteria.limit_shared: Demand the row-limit reference as the top-level LimitCount while tolerating extra PARAM tokens with the same number elsewhere. All positions share the one LIMIT binding; reuse needs no justification.
criteria.review_needed: This material cannot settle limit exclusivity, or neither alternative upholds the contracts.

limit_exclusivity.instructions: Decide if the row-limit number stays exclusive to LIMIT or may recur in other parameter slots. Consult common with topics.limit_exclusivity.

criteria.allow_trivia: Accept on a lone RawStmt and carry every leading and trailing semicolon, comment, and blank byte into the segments untouched. Statements lifted from consoles pass unchanged.
criteria.clean_ending: Accept on a lone RawStmt only when zero ASCII_59, SQL_COMMENT, or C_COMMENT tokens begin at or beyond the close of the final remaining token. Opening trivia survives; closing semicolons and comments fail.
criteria.review_needed: This material cannot settle trailing trivia, or neither alternative upholds the contracts.

trailing_semicolon.instructions: Decide if closing semicolons and comments persist into segments or fail the descriptor. Consult common with topics.trailing_semicolon.

fixed_constraints: P12 mandates a single statement in each descriptor: SELECT carrying the row-limit parameter as its top-level LIMIT for one/optional/many, versus INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE lacking RETURNING for execute. Application parameters run dense $1..$N in parameter-record field order, with the row-limit parameter as number N+1. Scanner offsets dice unchanging bytes into template pieces; no alternate SQL lexer exists.

Manifest validation already pins row_limit_parameter at len(parameters)+1 for row-returning shapes and bans it for execute. canlc validates every descriptor a single time per build; the frozen results feed I35 call lowering, which sources LIMIT from max_rows or 2.

Observed server conduct on PostgreSQL 17.11 via Bun 1.4.2 extended protocol: closing semicolons, closing blanks, and closing comments all run; paired statements die with cannot insert multiple commands into a prepared statement; a LIMIT number doubled as a filter runs with a single bound value in both places.

Upstream extent facts: RawStmt StmtLen reads 0 absent a closing semicolon, forcing statement ends to come from scanner tokens. Semicolons lex as ASCII_59; remarks lex as SQL_COMMENT or C_COMMENT; SELECT 1 plus arbitrary closing semicolons still parses as one RawStmt.
common.purpose: Guide the Can compiler using only the material handed over in this request. No web lookups, no coding, no prose answers. If the material leaves contenders indistinguishable, take the flagged uncertainty option.

limit_exclusivity.facts: P12 names the top-level LIMIT the distinct parameter following the application parameters. Given parameters [term] with limit 2, a query limiting on $2 alone binds the I35 call-site figure once. A query additionally testing $2 funnels that same call-site figure into filtering unnoticed. The server runs either form; only compile-time rules tell purpose apart from slip.

trailing_semicolon.facts: Writers paste SQL complete with closing semicolons and remarks from interactive tools. The server absorbs every flavor of closing trivia while separately refusing true multi-statement text. Tightening here merely narrows accepted static bytes; runtime stays safe regardless because pieces keep bytes intact and values remain bound.
